claim: A market title alone does not specify all contractual settlement rules.
limitations: This is a documented venue example; retain each actual contract's rules.

claim: An exceptional documented Polymarket outcome can redeem each side at 0.50 rather than forcing a binary payout.
limitations: Not a claim that every venue or contract uses the same exceptional resolution.

claim: The identification of average beliefs from an equilibrium price depends on trader and market assumptions.
limitations: Average belief is not objective event probability; full model proofs not inspected.

claim: Actual venue fee treatment can depend on price and market rather than a universal flat fee.
limitations: Mutable product-specific examples; no timeless fee table is asserted.

claim: Wolfers and Zitzewitz describe sufficient conditions for price to reflect mean beliefs and useful but sometimes biased approximations beyond those conditions.
limitations: Working paper; no blanket assertion that every market price is calibrated.

claim: Manski's risk-neutral price-taking model partially identifies central tendency and does not identify belief dispersion.
limitations: Model-dependent result; not evidence that prices are universally uninformative.

claim: The IEM study abstract compares 964 polls across five presidential elections and reports contemporaneous market vote-share predictions closer to the eventual two-party split in 74 percent of comparisons.
limitations: Five election outcomes are not 964 independent outcomes; vote-share accuracy is not net trading profit.

claim: Kalshi's inspected book schema represents YES and NO bids as string-valued dollar prices and fixed-point quantities.
limitations: Current schema only; recheck before acquisition.

claim: The inspected Kalshi guide derives an ordinary binary YES ask from one minus the best NO bid.
limitations: Subject to ordinary binary mechanics and displayed size; not a guaranteed delayed fill.

claim: Hanson's abstract describes market scoring rules as combining individual elicitation with group information aggregation.
limitations: Full cost-function theorem not inspected; classroom algebra should be derived independently.

claim: Polymarket documents disputes and additional-context clarifications after trading begins.
limitations: Do not infer exact payout or timing from an informal title.

claim: The inspected operator guide describes pUSD as a Polygon collateral wrapper representing a USDC claim.
limitations: Operator description is not an independent reserve or contract audit; separate regional products.

claim: The retrieved polymarket.com page displayed a U.S. trading block and directed users to a separate polymarket.us product.
limitations: Complete operative terms not exposed; no full eligibility matrix or permission to trade established.

claim: NOAA's monthly CO2 file explicitly identifies early Scripps data and later NOAA-period observations.
limitations: The proposed extract restricts to 1975 onward rather than assuming a third-party redistribution license.

claim: NOAA GML qualifies public-domain government-server information with attribution and no-endorsement requirements and separately discusses third-party data.
locator: Data and Products; Disclaimer of Endorsement
limitations: Public URL alone is not a license for unrelated or third-party data.

claim: Kalshi partitions live and historical records using moving cutoffs with object-specific timestamp meanings.
limitations: The documented interface does not establish a complete historical order-book archive.

claim: NOAA warns that quality-control checks may revise the published CO2 values.
limitations: Chronological splitting of a current vintage does not recover historical publication vintages.

claim: A study with many poll comparisons can still contain only a few independent election outcomes.
locator: IEM abstract: five elections and 964 polls
limitations: The distinction is a design interpretation of the reported sampling structure; no new effective-sample-size estimate is claimed.

claim: The calibration paper reports miscalibration in studied modern neural classifiers and effective temperature scaling on most examined datasets.
limitations: Image/document benchmarks; no automatic transfer to event markets.

claim: The beta-calibration abstract warns that isotonic calibration can overfit small datasets and logistic calibration can worsen some probability estimates.
limitations: Method and dataset conditions matter; no universally best calibration method established.

claim: Coordinate-descent regularization paths can fit logistic and multinomial models with lasso, ridge and elastic-net penalties.
limitations: Computation is distinct from leakage-safe model selection and forecasting benefit.

claim: The inspected Bayesian logistic-regression abstract proposes scaled predictors and Student-t coefficient priors and discusses complete separation.
limitations: A proposed weakly informative default is not a universal optimal prior.

claim: The author-maintained random-forest explanation uses bootstrap samples and random candidate feature subsets when growing classification trees.
locator: Berkeley author site: Overview and tree construction
limitations: Author explanatory sections inspected rather than original journal proofs; votes need calibration assessment.

claim: The XGBoost abstract describes sparse-data processing and weighted quantile sketches for scalable boosting.
limitations: Scalable benchmark performance does not establish event-market advantage.

claim: Cox's abstract models censored failure times with covariate effects multiplying an unspecified baseline hazard.
limitations: Occurrence time and settlement time differ; proportional-hazard assumptions require justification.

claim: The online changepoint preprint computes a posterior over current run length under independent before-and-after segment parameters.
limitations: Preprint; change detection is not causal identification or proof of a tradable regime.

claim: A bag-of-words representation discards word order while retaining term occurrence information.
limitations: Representation alone supplies no evidence of market predictive value.

claim: Inverse document frequency uses the number of documents containing a term rather than merely its total count.
limitations: Estimate corpus statistics within the training information boundary.

claim: BERT's inspected abstract describes bidirectional text pretraining followed by task-specific fine-tuning.
limitations: Language-task results do not verify a historical model's information cutoff.

claim: The attention paper compares complexity, sequential operations and dependency path length across attention, recurrent and convolutional layers.
limitations: Inspected later author HTML version; translation architecture evidence is not event-probability calibration evidence.

claim: The LSTM abstract addresses decaying error flow in recurrent learning and reports artificial sequence experiments.
limitations: Does not establish superiority on sparse market-event labels.

claim: Gneiting and Ranjan analyze predictive-distribution aggregation through coherence, calibration and dispersion.
limitations: Earlier manuscript abstract checked against published metadata; averaging alone does not establish calibration.

claim: Yao and colleagues extend stacking to Bayesian predictive distributions in an M-open setting.
limitations: Leave-one-out machinery is not automatically valid chronological evaluation.

claim: Domain-adversarial training uses labeled source and unlabeled target data to encourage task-discriminative but domain-indiscriminate features.
limitations: Not a universal guarantee of transfer across market families or regimes.

claim: The documented public CLOB response includes price and size levels and trading constraints such as tick size and minimum order size.
locator: Fetch an Order Book: API response example
limitations: A quote is not a fill guarantee; rights and freshness must be checked separately.

claim: The inspected Kalshi historical endpoint list covers markets, candles and trades but does not establish full historical order-book or queue coverage.
limitations: Absence from this inspected list is a limitation of established evidence, not a claim that no other authorized archive exists.

claim: Bailey and colleagues propose a probability-of-backtest-overfitting framework with combinatorially symmetric cross-validation implementations.
limitations: Not a universal cure for dependent event data; journal publication is 2017.

claim: The original false-discovery-rate paper's inspected abstract states a control result for independent test statistics.
limitations: Do not extend the claim to arbitrary dependence or invalid input p-values.

claim: Confidence sequences offer simultaneous-in-time coverage under stated process conditions, with a filtration and conditional-expectation estimand made explicit.
limitations: Time-uniformity does not remove process assumptions, leakage, selection or repeated-event dependence.

claim: An event container can group related markets without every such group being mutually exclusive.
limitations: Shared grouping alone does not prove an exhaustive partition or rule equivalence.

claim: The convex-market-design abstract treats bounded-payoff securities through convex cost functions and convex-hull optimization.
limitations: Institutional mechanism design is not proof of executable basket arbitrage.

claim: Market-dependent fees and rounding distinguish modeled spread revenue from actual net receipts.
limitations: This operational observation does not validate any market-making model or profit estimate.

claim: Settlement timing can vary with data availability and review, and actual settlement processing can involve net positions and rounding.
limitations: A product-specific operational example, not a quantified capital-lockup model.

claim: The doubly robust policy-evaluation abstract addresses differences between logged and target action distributions using reward and behavior-policy models.
limitations: Passive market observations are not automatically suitable action-reward logs; support assumptions remain necessary.

claim: The fixed-batch RL paper reports extrapolation problems when data differ from the current policy distribution and proposes batch-constrained behavior.
limitations: Continuous-control experiments do not establish execution simulator fidelity or trading profit.

claim: Kalshi's demo uses mock funds and separate credentials and warns that market price and behavior may not reflect real markets.
limitations: Mechanics validation only; no live-liquidity claim.

claim: Convex market design and predictive-distribution aggregation are established research areas relevant to proposed consistency and pooling hypotheses.
limitations: These sources establish related work, not novelty or profitability of a proposed research idea.

claim: A real NOAA CO2 extract can support a retrospective forecast-scoring exercise but does not supply historical market quotes or first-release vintages.
limitations: Study design recommendation, not a reported experiment result or proof of a market edge.

claim: NOAA's current-vintage monthly source includes interpolation flags and a documented 2022-2023 measurement-location change.
limitations: Preserve calendar gaps, exclusions and source-version limitations rather than treating all rows as comparable as-of observations.

claim: Compatible outcome-token mappings and contract rules must be checked before interpreting an event grouping as a basket.
limitations: A grouping or natural-language similarity alone does not establish executable arbitrage.

claim: A demo experiment cannot establish live market-making behavior when the provider explicitly warns its price and behavior may differ.
limitations: No simulated profit should be reported as historical executable performance.

claim: The retrieved geographic notice distinguishes polymarket.com from polymarket.us while leaving full operative terms unverified.
limitations: No individualized eligibility determination, geographic bypass or funded execution is authorized.

claim: A strictly proper scoring rule uniquely rewards the generating forecast distribution in expectation within the specified forecast class.
limitations: Source uses higher-is-better rewards; an expectation-level property does not certify finite-sample calibration or trading profit.

claim: The categorical quadratic and logarithmic scores are strictly proper in the inspected categorical representation.
locator: Section 3.1; Theorem 2 and Examples 1 and 3; pp. 362-363
limitations: Negate the source reward for a loss; the two-component binary squared-error sum is twice this book's single-YES convention.

claim: Direct comparisons of forecast scores should use the same set of forecast situations to avoid confounding performance with intrinsic predictability.
limitations: This does not establish independence of repeated observations or automatically justify any weighting scheme.

claim: An outcome-dependent normalized skill score is not automatically proper merely because its underlying score is proper.
limitations: Distinguish raw proper losses from normalized sample skill measures and retain the exact normalization assumptions.

claim: Fitting a calibration map on the base model's own fitting examples can introduce bias; the inspected experiment uses independent calibration examples.
limitations: The original random-sample design does not itself solve chronological or event-group leakage.

claim: Calibration benefits and harms differ by learning method and calibration sample size in the eight studied binary-classification problems.
locator: Author PDF pp. 2-3 and 8; Figure 8 discussion and Section 7
limitations: No universal ranking; 2005 neural-network experiments must not be generalized to all modern architectures.

claim: Back-propagation computes weight derivatives through repeated applications of the chain rule in a differentiable network.
limitations: The inspected objective is squared error; derivatives do not guarantee globally optimal fitting, calibration or market skill.

claim: The back-propagation article explicitly notes that local minima prevent a guarantee of finding a global minimum.
locator: Nature p. 535; local-minimum discussion, visually inspected
limitations: Do not substitute an illustrative representation-learning result for an event-market validation.

claim: The forecast-combination paper's abstract describes using past errors to weight two airline-passenger forecast sets and says the combination can reduce mean-square error.
locator: Primary publisher ScholarlyArticle abstract in raw HTML
limitations: Possibility in a point-forecast example, not guaranteed improvement or calibration of combined probabilities.

claim: White's Reality Check compares the best expected candidate performance in a specified search family with a benchmark.
limitations: Evaluating only the selected winner does not represent the searched family; correct trial records are required.

claim: White's inspected dependent bootstrap uses common geometrically distributed blocks and centers candidate performance differences for a least-favorable-null comparison.
limitations: Stationarity, strong mixing, block-length behavior and other asymptotic regularity conditions are substantive assumptions; not all Appendix proofs inspected.

claim: The stationary-bootstrap abstract describes random geometric block lengths and conditionally stationary resampled pseudo-series for weakly dependent stationary observations.
limitations: No original full-proof audit or particular event-data block length is established.

claim: Informational adverse selection can create a positive spread even for a risk-neutral specialist making zero expected transaction profits.
locator: Author reprint abstract and Section 1 opening; PDF pp. 1-3, visually inspected
limitations: Specialist-stock-market model with zero transaction costs and no binding inventory/cash constraints; not an observed prediction-market spread.

claim: The specialist's buy and sell valuations condition on information revealed by the direction of the incoming trade.
locator: Author reprint Section 1; PDF p. 3, visually inspected
limitations: A mechanism for fill-conditioned beliefs, not a measured adverse-selection effect for any specific venue.

claim: Avellaneda-Stoikov's main setup uses driftless arithmetic-Brownian stock prices, exponential terminal-wealth utility and distance-dependent Poisson arrivals.
limitations: Stock-model analogy; unbounded prices and terminal marking differ from bounded event payouts and settlement jumps.

claim: The simple reservation-price and spread expressions in equations 29-30 are approximate quotes under symmetric exponential arrival rates.
limitations: Do not call this the exact general HJB solution; the paper focuses on inventory risk rather than a full adverse-selection model.

claim: The Avellaneda-Stoikov strategy comparisons are numerical simulations under specified parameters, not historical executable-return backtests.
limitations: Costless quote changes, one-share fills and terminal midpoint marking omit real execution frictions; no live-market profit inference.

claim: Kelly distinguishes expected log-growth from expected capital and shows that repeated all-in bets can lead to eventual ruin despite attractive expected capital.
locator: The gambler with a private wire; pp. 918-920
limitations: Repeated-bet model assumptions matter; this is not a finite-horizon safety guarantee for estimated probabilities.

claim: Kelly's conclusion limits the stated dominance comparison to fixed allocations per received symbol and identifies reinvestment and stake control as essential.
limitations: The paper explicitly leaves broader time-dependent policy comparisons open and supplies no universal safe fractional-Kelly rule.

claim: Kelly's track-take treatment permits retaining capital rather than betting the entire bankroll.
locator: When there is a track take; pp. 923-925
limitations: The general case assumes independent transmitted symbols and noise; venue fees, correlated contracts and capital lockup require their own model.

claim: Kyle's abstract specifies a single risk-neutral insider, random noise traders and competitive risk-neutral market makers.
locator: Complete primary Econometric Society abstract in raw HTML
limitations: Its continuous-limit equilibrium properties are not empirical laws of event prices or evidence about any particular counterparty.
